Yes, on `dev`. Most workflows switched to Blacksmith today (2026-10-19) in `1b383c749`, "Migrate workflows to Blacksmith runners (#228)". They now run on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. That covers ci, mailfn-release, reviewfn-release, publish-tag (first job), pullfrog, the searchfn tests, the docs Cloudflare deploy and routes workflows, the uifn catalogs preview, and the uifn phase-14 compat jobs.

These still run on other runners on `dev`:
- **GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`:** `apifn-api-check.yml`, both jobs in `publish-python.yml`, and the second job in `publish-tag.yml`.
- **`macos-latest`:** `release-swift.yml`.
- **Self-hosted:** the browser matrix jobs in `uifn-phase-14-compat.yml` (`["self-hosted","uifn-phase14",...]`).

Your local branch `next` doesn't have the migration yet, so its workflows still say `ubuntu-latest` / `ubuntu-24.04`. Merging `dev` into it will bring the change in.

content.text:
Blacksmith isn't free for this repo; the free tier stops at 3,000 minutes a month. I opened a PR to switch back to GitHub-hosted runners: https://github.com/21nCo/superfunctions/pull/250

**Blacksmith:** The free tier is 3,000 minutes a month with no credit card. There's also an open-source program you apply for through a form. They want an actively maintained public repo, a permissive license and clear community use, but they don't publish what the program actually gives you. The repo is public, so GitHub-hosted runners are already free here with no minute cap, and our CI would pass 3,000 minutes quickly.

**The PR:** It undoes #228 on a branch off `dev`. All 11 workflows #228 touched go back to `ubuntu-latest` (or `ubuntu-24.04` for the uifn phase-14 compat jobs), and back to `actions/checkout` instead of `useblacksmith/checkout`. The diff only changes those lines, and every workflow file still parses as YAML. CI hasn't run on the PR yet.

**Namespace:** No. There's no free allowance and no open-source program, just pay-per-use after a 30-day trial.

**CircleCI:** It does have a free open-source tier, up to about 400,000 credits a month for Linux builds on public repos (its older support pages say 100,000 a week instead). But it's a separate CI system, not a runner for GitHub Actions. We'd have to rewrite every workflow in CircleCI's own config format. I don't think it's worth it while GitHub-hosted runners cost us nothing.

The one case for keeping Blacksmith is speed, and you could apply to their open-source program for that. I can do that instead if you'd rather keep it.

Sources:
- [Blacksmith pricing](https://www.blacksmith.sh/pricing)
- [Blacksmith docs](https://docs.blacksmith.sh/)
- [Namespace pricing](https://namespace.so/pricing)
- [Namespace GitHub Actions](https://namespace.so/docs/solutions/github-actions)
- [CircleCI credits docs](https://circleci.com/docs/credits)
- [CircleCI pricing](https://circleci.com/pricing/)
- [CircleCI public/private repo credits](https://support.circleci.com/en/articles/15091242-how-does-circleci-charge-credits-for-private-and-public-repositories)
